title: Burden, Standard of Proof and Decision Timing — Unemployment Insurance Appeals Bench Book Schedule
content:
Under **Unemployment Insurance Appeals**, each docket names the party that must prove the disputed fact, the standard the evidence must meet, the calendar days after filing within which the decision is targeted, whether the decision may send the case back for a new hearing, and — for the Board of Review — the calendar days after the Board decision is mailed within which court review may be sought (0 means not applicable).

| Docket | Burden of proof | Standard of proof | Decision targeted within (calendar days after filing) | Remand for a new hearing allowed | Court review deadline (calendar days after the Board decision is mailed) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue | the employer for a discharge; the claimant for a quit | preponderance of the evidence | 30 | no | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue | the claimant | preponderance of the evidence | 30 | no | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination | the claimant | preponderance of the evidence | 30 | no | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud | the agency | preponderance of the evidence, and clear and convincing evidence for a fraud finding | 45 | no | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge | the employer | preponderance of the evidence | 45 | no | 0 |
| Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate | the employer | preponderance of the evidence | 90 | no | 0 |
| Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review | the appellant | preponderance of the evidence | 75 | yes | 30 |

## Schedule notes

- On the Separation Issue docket the burden follows the kind of separation: where the claimant was discharged the employer must prove the disputed fact, and where the claimant quit the claimant must.
- On the Overpayment and Fraud docket the agency carries the burden; a fraud finding must meet the clear and convincing standard, the rest of the case the preponderance standard.
- Only the Board of Review may remand; only a Board of Review decision has a court review deadline (30 calendar days).
